commentary_segments.text: The BiCMOS opamp which operates at a supply voltage below 1 V is shown in this slide. It uses a pseudo-differential input stage. This is easy, as the input voltages are connected to the V ’s BE of the bandgap. Actually, the input transistors form current mirrors with the diode connected npn transistors of the bandgap reference. The currents are now well defined! The outputs of the input transistors lead to the output through one or two current mirrors. It is therefore a single-stage opamp. The gain is moderate, but the dominant pole is high, as indicated by the GBW. The minimum supply voltage is V +V . For a V of about 0.5 V this is only about 0.9 V. GS DSsat T

commentary_text: The BiCMOS opamp which operates at a supply voltage below 1 V is shown in this slide. It uses a pseudo-differential input stage. This is easy, as the input voltages are connected to the V ’s BE of the bandgap. Actually, the input transistors form current mirrors with the diode connected npn transistors of the bandgap reference. The currents are now well defined! The outputs of the input transistors lead to the output through one or two current mirrors. It is therefore a single-stage opamp. The gain is moderate, but the dominant pole is high, as indicated by the GBW. The minimum supply voltage is V +V . For a V of about 0.5 V this is only about 0.9 V. GS DSsat T
